draft.title: Fascism in Italy
card: After the First World War, Italy faced unemployment, rising prices and strikes. Many Italians felt let down by the peace settlement and feared communism. Liberal governments looked weak.

Benito Mussolini led the Fascist Party. Its armed squads, the Blackshirts, attacked socialists, trade unionists and their offices. This violence made the Fascists feared, and it also won support from people who wanted order.

In October 1922 the Fascists marched towards Rome and demanded power. King Victor Emmanuel III did not order the army to stop them. He asked Mussolini to form a government, so Mussolini took office legally, under threat of force.
Mussolini then built a one-party state. He took the title Il Duce, passed laws that gave him wide powers, and banned other parties. By the late 1920s Italy was a dictatorship.
draft.remember: Mussolini gained office through force and pressure, then used his office to build a one-party dictatorship.

a.q: How did Mussolini become prime minister of Italy in 1922?
opts: The king asked him to form a government after the march
He won a majority of seats in a national election
The army overthrew the government and installed him
Parliament made him dictator before the march began
a.why: The March on Rome put pressure on the government, and the king chose to ask Mussolini to form a government rather than use the army against him. He did not win an election or take power in an army coup. His dictatorial powers came later, after he held office.
a.clue: Think about who had the power to appoint a prime minister.

b.q: Which statement best explains why the March on Rome led to Mussolini taking power?
opts: The king did not stop the march and asked him to govern
The army fought the Fascists and lost near Rome
The Blackshirts took Rome by force and removed the king
The Fascists had already banned all other parties
b.why: The march worked because the king did not use the army against it and invited Mussolini to form a government. The Fascists did not defeat the army, because it was never ordered to fight. Banning other parties came after Mussolini took office, as he built the one-party state.
b.clue: Consider what the king did when the Fascists threatened Rome.

a.best: The king asked him to form a government after the march

b.best: The king did not stop the march and asked him to govern

problems.detail: 'Gained office through force and pressure' drops the card's point that he took office legally when the king appointed him under threat of force. Students could read it as a violent seizure of power.

'After the march' is slightly imprecise. The king invited Mussolini on 29 October, while the Blackshirts were still gathering outside Rome, before they entered the city. 'During' or 'in response to the march' would be more accurate.

check.summary: The facts and answers are sound. The remember line loses the card's point that Mussolini was appointed legally under threat of force, and option a's 'after the march' is slightly loose on timing.
